$comment: The pin manifest. A build is in this repository iff a TRACKED file of Archipelago-CC names it; scripts/procgen/check-seedling-wasm-pins.mjs in that repo gates the FOUR-way agreement between this manifest, the .gitignore whitelist, what git actually tracks here, and the build names that repo’s tracked files actually spell. Every build directory carries exactly four files. `js`/`wasm` are the AUTHORITY on the payload filenames — they do not always match the directory name. `capabilities` is the BUILD-SIDE HALF OF FEATURE DETECTION (⚖ user, 2026-08-29): the host decides from DATA whether a feature applies, never from an opt-in flag, so a build DECLARES what its ActionScript can do and the panel looks the entry up by the directory name its preset points at. It is MANDATORY and an empty array is a real answer — absence would be indistinguishable from “measured, none”. The vocabulary is declared ONCE, in the consumer (Archipelago-CC frontend/modules/flashPanel/seedlingRandomizerEligibility.js WASM_BUILD_CAPABILITIES), and check-seedling-wasm-pins.mjs imports it rather than spelling a second copy, so a typo cannot pass as “this build does not have it”. ⚖⚖ THE MANIFEST-PROSE EXEMPTION (ruled by the user 2026-08-30, EDITOR INTEGRATION slice P4): a gitlink bump whose submodule diff touches ONLY this file AND whose per-build payload md5s are byte-identical owes the pins gate plus the bounded reach, NOT the full-tier drive — the md5 identity is QUOTED in the outer commit as the licence. It is written where the OWED gate reads (Archipelago-CC scripts/procgen/check-seedling-full-tier-owed.mjs, which is what prices the tier) and restated here because this is the file the edit claiming it is made in. ⛔ THE BOUNDARY IS THE PREMISE, and it is all three clauses: touch a build directory, an md5 field or the .gitignore whitelist in the same commit and the exemption does not apply — a payload that moved is a different game, which is exactly what only the full tier can see.

builds.note: Phase 4c — THE bot build from R9 slice 12g′ (2026-08-26). It differs from p4b in ONE behaviour and the behaviour is an ARM TIME, not a game rule: botStart no longer sets `armed = true; tick = 0` beside the world swap it requests. `FP.world = x` writes FP._goto only (FP.as:87-90) and the swap lands in Engine.checkWorld() at the END of the next Engine.update() (Engine.as:77, :242-252), while Main.update() runs Bot.update() ABOVE super.update() (Main.as:61-66) — so exactly ONE Bot.update ran against the OUTGOING world (the BOOT_PRESWAP_FRAMES = 1 law, r7Acceptance.js:652). If that world was still fading the frame was counted dead and nothing was lost; if its fade had ended, t=0 was RECORDED off a player about to be discarded and every tape input landed a frame off. Slice 12g measured the cut to ONE FRAME (19 wins at outgoing frame ≤ 18, 8 losses at ≥ 19, 27 drives, no overlap) and proved it is a FRAME COUNT and not a duration: 0.48 s of pre-boot idle produced both outcomes. p4c arms in Bot.update on the first frame where FP.world IS the instance botStart constructed. ⛔ THE TWO OBVIOUS CONDITIONS ARE BOTH VACUOUS and a reader will reach for them: Game's ctor runs `level = _level` (Game.as:630) and `playerPosition = new Point(...)` (:631), and both are setters onto STATICS — Main.level (:526-528) and Main.playerPositionX/Y (:555-561) — so `Main.level == bootLevel && atBootPosition()` is already true while the swap is still only FP._goto, and a build gated on it would have been a NO-OP. Object identity on FP.world is not a proxy for the observation's source: `FP.world as Game` feeds the dead-frame gate and findPlayer() is FP.world.classFirst(Player). ⚠ TWO OBSERVABLE CONSEQUENCES, both intended: the waiting frame is NOT counted in dead_frames (the tape has not started), so dead_frames on a swapping tape is the new world's fade alone — uniform, where p4b read that plus one on the winning path; and botStatus gains `arm: {pending, armed_at}`, the arm frame in Game.time units, which is what makes a driver-side arm bound's perturbation measurable at all. The RNG is unmoved: Rng.setState stays below the `new Game` line and the swap lands on the same frame as before.

builds.note: Phase 4d — EDITOR INTEGRATION slice M1 (2026-08-28), and ⛔ NOT A DEFAULT: p4c still holds every SEEDLING_PAGE default, WASM_PAGE, the three presets' flash_panel.wasm and both tests that assert the name. Making p4d the default is a SEPARATE decision that moves 53 tracked files / 69 lines. It is the first build to carry anything the host reads beyond the vanilla item flags. ⛓ Pickups/APItem.as is built from an `<apitem tag= look=>` element the host writes into a delivered level set, GRANTS NOTHING, and calls Game.setPersistence(tag, false) on collection — `false`, the engine's own collected marker, because buildLevelPersistence fills the table with `true` meaning “nothing cleared”. Its sprite comes from a look → [PNG, frameW, frameH] table of sixteen RE-EMBEDDED graphics plus the shared Game.bossKeys[N]; re-embedded and not borrowed from a throwaway vanilla instance because Chest's own field initialiser calls Rng.cos() and would move the RNG stream every tape is recorded against. ⛓ `look == "ap"` binds a plain Image where every Seedling look binds a Spritemap, which is what makes the placeholder observable with no pixels at all: botMobiles reports `frame` as `graphic as Spritemap`, null for the logo and a number for a Seedling sprite. ⛓ The two seams are `<seq>|`-prefixed strings on the EXISTING BridgeGeneric channel — no bridge change, no re-injection change, no addCallback — declared BEFORE `level` in games/seedling.json, because BridgeGeneric builds its property list in declaration order and reports in it. ⚠ The seq prefix is load-bearing: a property is reported only when its value CHANGED, measured on p4c with an existing String static before a line of this was compiled. ⛔ FLAGS OFF IS BYTE-INERT: with no level set delivered and no external door, the only observable difference from p4c is the DECLARED property set — the four new properties present and empty/zero.
